The disk-exhaustion chain is confirmed by a metric time series, not just logs: ledger-db disk_used_pct climbs monotonically 78.16% (11:00Z) → 100.0% (14:55-14:58Z bucket, missing_points 0), with 2-min resolution showing 98.73% at 14:46 and 99.93% at 14:56 [F25,F26,F27,F33]; cpu_pct (~30%), connections_active (~62) and slow_queries_per_min (~1) are flat, so disk is the only measurable exhausted resource [F28,F29,F24]. Temporal order is established and the cause precedes onset tightly: the fill began at/before 11:00Z — ~3h48m before the 14:46Z dep-6203 deploy — and slot WAL retention is visible from 12:19:34Z [F30,F31,F32,F33,F34]. Scope is consistent: 3 of 4 direct ledger-db writers (payment ~60-63%, settlement ~54-56%, order ~47-48%) break in the same 14:55-14:58 buckets with the identical PG storage signature [F7,F8,F9,F19,F20,F10], covering services the deploy never touched. Alternatives are contradicted by evidence rather than dismissed: H2/H4 by the actual error text ('could not extend file: No space left on device', not a validation rejection), the identical failure of non-deploy recipients (settlement/order), and non-recovery after rollback [F9,F16,F19,F20]; H3 by PG storage error + no kafka change [F13]; H4 also by flat cpu/connections/slow_queries and a pre-deploy multi-hour ramp [F26,F28,F29]. Remaining gaps are confirmatory only and do not change the ranking: portfolio-service's immunity (F21,F22) is a write-pattern detail that worsens nothing for the single-shared-volume origin — H5 (cluster/shared-host) is weakened by F2 placing all three failing writers on ledger-db and by no evidence of any second datastore or host volume; the exact slot-stop instant is unobservable (no slot-level metric, logs only from 11:00Z [F32,F35]) but the deploy-independence conclusion holds regardless. Cap 0.88 rather than higher: the H1 chain's 'sole exhausted resource' claim cannot exclude an unmeasurable IOPS mechanism (no such metric exists [F24]), portfolio-service's immunity is unexplained by any telemetry, and the exact fill origin predates the observable window; H1 also still lists F23 (unverified inference) as support.

challenges.issue: H1's supporting list includes F23, an UNVERIFIED/inference finding; it is not load-bearing (F7/F8/F19/F20 carry the blast-radius claim), but it should be demoted so the citation set contains only verified findings.

portfolio-service, a fourth direct ledger-db writer, is completely unaffected (flat ~0.2% error_rate, zero ERROR logs, zero 'No space left on device' matches) and no telemetry explains why. H1 assumes a read-mostly/dormant write pattern; this is unproven and is the one scope anomaly in an otherwise clean fan-in story.

The 'disk is the sole exhausted resource' claim is bounded by the metric set: no IOPS/disk-throughput metric exists for ledger-db (F24), and the exact start of the fill predates the observable window (already 78.16% at 11:00Z, logs only from 11:00Z, no slot-level metric [F32,F35]). The disk-full → write-failure mechanism is directly evidenced (F10,F27), but the pre-window origin is inferred, not measured.

H5 remains untested rather than refuted: whether order-service's orders table physically resides on the ledger-db volume was never confirmed (only inferred from the F2 fan-in list). Given identical onset and error text, the single-shared-volume reading is far better supported, but the physical-placement confirmation was never retrieved and is now moot for the chosen fix.
Recovery evidence (does dropping the analytics_cdc slot / freeing space restore error rates) is absent, so the final 'fix works' link is inferred from HIST-114 rather than observed in this incident.
